log.msg: BIG CUT: the blog wears the SITE shell, not a hand-rolled one. page topic flex fill + core/Sidebar + .pages is exactly what /framework/ uses, so the two-level rail, the burger below 52em, and derived active/in-path all came free. One 6-line Sidebar subclass (BlogNav) makes a group TITLE a link, which is what lets .in-path light a section. Saved ~150 lines of the blogx lab CSS and the blog looks like the rest of the site.

Cards are Page.css .page-previews - the same wall /framework/ and the homepage use. Only .blog-card-date is the blogs own. The magazine front is then just: hero (display type in cqw) | wall (--column 17em, 24em past 120em) + a topics rail, in a 0.95:1.55 grid above 60em of ROW.

TRAP AVOIDED: a display utility on the region default box would have won by LAYER over Page.css theme rule .pages > .default {display:none} and left the front on screen under every section and post - the util arrangement contract only covers .page elements. The magazine is a box INSIDE .default, not .default itself.

COORDINATOR BLOCKER 1 FIXED and verified. Post.render() had div.c(blog-read, () => { this.head(); this.read(); }) - a block-bodied arrow that DROPS the promise md.file() returns, so every single-part post rendered an empty column with zero console errors. A multi-part post hid it: its read() renders a child Page which appends itself as a side effect. Now `return this.read()`. Verified: all four single-part posts (dashboard 3369, hello-lew42 3256, layout-generators 4432, claude-tooling 4663, panel-playground 3217 chars of prose) AND the two-part how-this-blog-works (3486, both parts route).

COORDINATOR BLOCKER 2 FIXED. Every manifest entry now carries image:, meta.mjs falls back to the first PNG in the post dir when one is omitted, and all ten shells are re-stamped - curl of /blog/framework/how-this-blog-works/ returns og:image + twitter:card summary_large_image in the raw bytes. ⚠ ONE DESIGN CALL: the writers each embed their PNG in their own prose, so drawing image: at the top of the post as R1 did would print the same screenshot twice. image: is the SOCIAL CARD now; `lead: true` is the opt-in that also draws it at the top, and the front-post flag was renamed lead: -> featured: so one word does not mean two things (a `lead` field would also have shadowed the lead() method - the trap core hit with `opens`).

FRONT HEIGHT, measured twice. Top-anchored the whole magazine was 403px of a 3440x1440 fold - 72% of the screen white BELOW a finished composition, which reads as still-loading. Centred it is 1332 of 1440 at 3440 and 984 of 1080 at 1920. The fix is align-self: stretch on the ONE default block, never align-items on the region: stretching the region also pinned every post page to the region height with its prose overflowing a 1440px box (measured 2382/1440).

RELAY 3 done: panel-playground description replaced with the true one (two wireframing tools, different mechanisms) and its index.html re-stamped - curl confirms the new og:description and the glob fallback picked panel-space.png.

⚠ THE :80 DEV SERVER IS DOWN (nothing listening; it was up at 12:01 and gone by 12:26 - not touched by this task). Final verification ran against a private PORT=8094 node server.js, stopped afterwards. 17 urls at 400/1920/3440: ZERO console errors, ZERO 4xx. All six posts render prose (3217-4663 chars); both parts of how-this-blog-works route; rail active/in-path correct at 2 and 3 depths.

assign.outcome:
**The real blog is live at [/blog/](/blog/)** — a magazine front, three sections, six posts, and one shell borrowed whole from the site.

![the front at 3440](front-3440.png)

**The structure.** `/blog/<section>/<post>/`, three sections, six posts, all in one manifest ([`posts.js`](/blog/posts.js)):

| | |
|---|---|
| [framework](/blog/framework/) | [Hello, lew42](/blog/framework/hello-lew42/) (3 parts) - [How this blog works](/blog/framework/how-this-blog-works/) (2 parts) |
| [systems](/blog/systems/) | [Generators: layouts and pages](/blog/systems/layout-generators/) - [Panel and Playground](/blog/systems/panel-playground/) |
| [ai](/blog/ai/) | [The AI dashboard](/blog/ai/dashboard/) - [MCP, Playwright, and skills](/blog/ai/claude-tooling/) |

**All six post dirs existed at verify time.** R1's test post moved to `/blog/framework/how-this-blog-works/`, canonical and og:url re-stamped.

**THE BIG CUT: the blog wears the SITE shell.** `page topic flex fill` + `core/Sidebar` + `.pages` is exactly what `/framework/` uses, so the two-level rail, the burger below 52em, the brand, the mode toggle and `.active`/`.in-path` all came free. Cards are Page.css's own `.page-previews`, so the blog adds no second kind of card to the site. What is left for `blog.css` is the composition. One 6-line `Sidebar` subclass makes a section title a LINK - a caption cannot carry `in-path`, which is the whole reason a post lives under a section. That is ~150 lines of the blogx lab's chrome CSS not written, and a blog that looks like the site.

**Measured, 17 urls at 400 / 1920 / 3440: zero console errors, zero 4xx.** The front fills 1332 of a 3440x1440 fold and 984 of 1080; the post reaches 90px from the right edge at 3440 (read 2680 + rail 243 in a 3166 region). Only `.pages` scrolls. og: tags curl-verified in the raw bytes at every new url, section indexes included.

**Two silent bugs fixed** (both relayed by the post writers):
- `div.c("blog-read", () => { this.head(); this.read(); })` - a block-bodied arrow that DROPS the promise `md.file()` returns. Every single-part post rendered an empty column with no error and no 404; the only post that existed was multi-part, whose `read()` appends a child Page as a side effect, so it was invisible for a whole build.
- `image:` is the SOCIAL CARD now, not also the picture at the top: each writer embeds their PNG in their own prose, so R1's coupling printed the same screenshot twice. `lead: true` is the opt-in, and the front's flag was renamed `lead:` -> `featured:` - one word for two things is also how a boolean shadows a method.

**One measurement worth keeping.** Top-anchored, the whole front was 403px of a 3440x1440 fold - 72% white BELOW a finished composition, which reads as still loading. Centred it is 1332/1440. The fix is `align-self: stretch` on the ONE default block, never `align-items` on the region: stretching the region also pinned every post page to the region height with its prose overflowing a 1440px box (2382/1440).

- Shots: [front 3440](front-3440.png) - [1920](front-1920.png) - [400](front-400.png) - [a section](section-framework-1920.png) - [a post at 3440](post-3440.png)
- Docs: [The front](/blog/doc/front/) (new) - [File structure](/blog/doc/structure/) - [Meta tags](/blog/doc/meta-tags/) - [Reading page](/blog/doc/reading-page/) - [readme](/blog/readme.md)

**FOR THE MASTERMIND - the homepage line.** `/blog/` is linked from nowhere. In `public/page.js`, into `sections`:

```js
{ title: "Blog", url: "/blog/", desc: "Working notes on the framework, the tools built on it, and the AI board that watches it get built." },
```

**Cuts, and what is left.**
- E2's "parts as columns" (#3) is not built: `how-this-blog-works` and `hello-lew42` swap parts in place, which is the shape that also works at 400. The columns treatment is a per-post opt-in somebody can add later.
- The topics rail is on the FRONT only. On a post it would be a third rail beside the nav and the post's own parts/ToC.
- A section with two posts still leaves empty slots in the wall at 3440 - the archive, not the layout, is the constraint.
- `how-this-blog-works/lead.png` is a screenshot of an older draft of its own page, and it is that post's og:image.
- ⚠ **The :80 dev server went down mid-task** (up at 12:01, gone by 12:26; not touched here). Verification ran against a private `PORT=8094`, since stopped.
